Shri Rajesh Joshi - learned Ga for the respondent/Stat
 Judgment

This Criminal Appeal under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is preferred being aggrieved by the judgment dated 26.02.2013 passed in S.T.No.124/2012 by the Additional Judge to the Court of First Additional Session Judge, Mandleshwar, District Khargone whereby the appellants have been convicted under Section 363 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo 3 years R.I.
with fine of Rs.500/- with default stipulation of additional one month R.I. 2 .

entities.text: Court of First Additional Session Judge, Mandleshwar, District Khargone
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts of the case in brief are that the appellants were put to trial with Ramdas.

Appellant Ramdas was charged under Section 363, 366, 376(2)(g) alternatively 376(1), 506 Part-II, 342 of the IPC for committing the rape with 17 years old prosecutrix (PW-1) after kidnapping her on 09.02.2012 at 04:00 pm regarding which Crime No.47/2012 was registered at NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17736 2 CRA-403-2013 Police Station Balakwada, District Khargone (M.P.).
3 .

The appellants abjured the guilt and claimed for trial and to bring home the guilt the prosecution examined as many as 11 witnesses including victim as PW-1, her father as PW-2, her mother as PW-3, Rameshwar Dongre - Head Master as PW-4, Dr. Amita Pandey as PW-6, Dattatray - A.S.I. as PW-7, Jitendra Singh Pawar - S.D.O. as PW-9, Dr. Satyam Tare - Govt. Doctor as PW-10, B.K.
Malviya - S.I. as PW-11.
4 . In examination under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure all the facts and circumstances are either denied or ignorance was expressed.
5 . Appreciating the evidence, the trial Court convicted and sentenced the appellants as mentioned in para 1 of the judgment.
They were acquitted from rest of the charges.

1 under Section 363 and 376(1) of the IPC and was sentenced to three years and seven years R.I. with fine of Rs.500/- and Rs.1,000/- with default stipulation.

sentences.text: Ramdas did not prefer to file the appeal.
The appellant no.1 Mahesh preferred this appeal on the ground that the victim (PW-1) was a consenting party.
She accompanied Ramdas on her own will and married to Ramdas.
The appellants have been convicted without evidence.
6 . Learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State has supported the conviction as well as sentence and prayed for dismissal of appeal.
Perused the record.

7 . The trial Court has recorded the finding in para no.12 of the judgment that the Victim (PW-1) was 17 years old on the basis of her date of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17736 3 CRA-403-2013 birth i.e. 23.07.1995 as per Exhibit-P/5 and the appellants have taken her from the place where she was taking care of her cattle of the field and thereafter appellant no.2 Kishore took her on motorcycle and thereafter she was carried to Indore by bus.

Jitendra Singh Pawar - S.D.O.
(PW-9) has collected the documents regarding date of birth of the victim and the documents regarding date of birth of the victim is in confirmity with the testimony of Victim (PW-1) in which she has stated that she has studied upto 9th standard.
She has stated the name of school and age as 17 years.

Accordingly, the findings of the trial Court that the victim was 17 years on the date of incident does not call for interference and she was female under 18 years of age as required under Section 361 of the IPC.

8 . The testimony of PW-1 established that the appellants were also involved in the act of taking her from place where she was taking care of their cattle and father (PW-2) and mother (PW-3) have deposed that she was taken from their lawful guardianship without their consent.
The cross- examination of these witnesses does not disclose any material that will affect their reliability.
Accordingly, the conviction of the appellants under Section 363 of the IPC does not require interference.
Now come to the question of sentence.
9 . It is argued that the trial Court has recorded the finding in para 29 that the appellants have no criminal antecedent.
10. Considering that the appellants have no criminal antecedent, purpose of sentencing will be served if their sentence is reduced to one year & three months R.I.

Hence, this criminal appeal is partly allowed and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17736 4 CRA-403-2013 maintaining the conviction punishable under Section 363 of the IPC, the sentence of the appellants is reduced from 3 years to 1 year & 3 (three) months R.I. and fine of Rs.500/- with default stipulation of one month R.I.
11.
Copy of the judgment be supplied to the appellants through Khargone Sub Jail, Mandleshwar.
Supersession warrant be prepared accordingly.
